RAJYA  SABHA
————
List of Questions for ORAL  ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Tuesday,  the July 25, 2006/Sravana 3, 1928 (Saka)
————
(Ministries: Civil Aviation; Company Affairs; Culture; Finance; Heavy
Industries and Public Enterprises; Petroleum and Natural Gas;
Tourism; Water Resources)
Total number of questions — 20
Training of probationers in National
Academy of Customs and Central
Excise
*21. MISS MABEL REBELLO: Will
the Minister of  FINANCE be pleased to
state:
(a) what efforts are being made to give
training to the probationers in the National
Academy of Customs and Central Excise,
Narcotics, Faridabad in the taxation law,
which are progressive and not regressive in
nature; and
(b) whether there is any proposal to
send the officers to the Indian Institutes of
Management (IIMs) compulsorily for a
management course to improve the system/
bureaucracy from within?
Retail expansion programme
of HPCL
*22. SHRI B.J. PANDA: Will the
Minister of  PETROLEUM AND
NATURAL GAS be pleased to state:
(a) whether Hindustan Petroleum
Corporation Ltd. (HPCL) proposes to
invest Rs. 1000 crores for its retail expansion
by March, 2007;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) the details of the outlets that would
be opened/upgraded in the State of Orissa?
Production under heavy industries
†*23. SHRI RAJ MOHINDER
SINGH MAJITHA:
DR. MURLI MANOHAR
JOSHI:
Will the Minister of  HEAVY
INDUSTRIES AND PUBLIC
ENTERPRISES be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that a number of
units are functioning as heavy industries in
the country;
(b) if so, the total number of such units
and the number of those units in which
production is going on at present; and
(c) the details of units in which
production has stopped and the Ministries
to which these units are attached?
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

8
Reforms package for FDI flow in
retail and insurance sector
*24. SHRIMATI SHOBHANA
BHARTIA: W ill the Minister of
FINANCE be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government after
completing two years in office has decided
to have a fresh package of reforms which
on implementation could see greater FDI
flow in retail and insurance sector as well
as reduce share holding of Government in
Nationalised banks;
(b) if so, whether all these proposals
have been considered; and
(c) the details of the same and by when,
it is likely to be implemented?
Regional air services of Alliance Air
*25. SHRIMATI SYEDA ANWARA
TAIMUR : Will the Minister of  CIVIL
AVIATION be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that shortage of
pilots has hit North Eastern Region air
operations and the Alliance Air is looking
for foreign pilots to operate the regional air
services;
(b) whether the Alliance Air is being
funded by the North East Council (NEC)
to operate the regional air services; and
(c) if so, the details thereof?
Improvement of facilities at airports
*26. SHRI T.T.V. DHINAKARAN:
Will the Minister of  CIVIL AVIATION be
pleased to state:
(a) the percentage of growth of domestic
air traffic in the country during the last
three years, year-wise;
(b) the details of investment in
infrastructure development in airports
during the last three years, year-wise;
(c) the reasons for the frequent delay in
take off/landing of aircrafts of national as
well as private carriers; and
(d) the steps taken to improve passenger
facilities that have suffered due to increase
in the volume of air traffic?
Upheaval in stock market
*27. SHRI GIREESH KUMAR
SANGHI:
SHRI RAJKUMAR DHOOT:
 Will the Minister of  FINANCE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have
ascertained the reasons of the recent
upheaval in the stock market;
(b) if so, whether it is a fact that one of
the major causes of such upheaval was large
scale selling by the Foreign Institutional
Investors (FIIs);
(c) if so, whether Government would
consider it safe to link social safety,
instruments like insurance and pension
schemes with uncertain equity market that
may deplete the returns; and
(d) what steps are being considered by
Government to insulate such schemes from
upheavals caused by speculative motives
of FIIs?
Development of tourism in North
Eastern States
†*28. SHRI MOTILAL VORA:
MS. SUSHILA TIRIYA:
 Will the Minister of TOURISM be
pleased to state:
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

9
(a) whether Government have any
scheme to attract local and foreign tourists
towards North Eastern States;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) the amount provided for the
development of tourism in the North
Eastern States; and
(d) the steps to be taken by
Government for the safety of tourists?
Funds for revival of sick PSUs
*29. DR. M.A.M. RAMASWAMY:
Will the Minister of  HEAVY INDUSTRIES
AND PUBLIC ENTERPRISES be pleased
to state:
(a) the total number of PSUs lying sick
in the Southern States, State-wise;
(b) whether Government have chalked
out any plan to revive these sick PSUs;
(c) if so, the details thereof;
(d) if not, the reasons therefor; and
(e) the total estimated funds required
for the revival of each of these PSUs?
Revision in prices of petroleum
products
*30. SHRI RAJKUMAR DHOOT:
SHRI JAI PARKASH
AGGARWAL:
 Will the Minister of  PETROLEUM
AND NATURAL GAS be pleased to
state:
(a) whether it is a fact that there has
been wide spread agitations against the
steep hike in price of petrol, diesel and
CNG effective June, 2006;
(b) whether Government have assessed
its impact on the prices of essential
commodities;
(c) if so, the details thereof and the action
proposed to be taken by Government to
ensure that prices are not unduly increased
by traders on the pretext of hike in rates of
petroleum products;
(d) whether Government have
considered other options such as reduction
in excise duty, sales tax, etc. so that
household budget of common man is not
badly affected; and
(e) if not, the reasons therefor?
Sale of kerosene at higher rates
*31. SHRI DARA SINGH: Will the
Minister of  PETROLEUM AND
NATURAL GAS be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are aware that
a large number of petrol pump owners and
kerosene dealers in the country are
indulging in irregularities;
(b) if so, the number of dealers who
have been punished during the last three
years, year-wise, till-date;
(c) whether a number of dealers of
kerosene oil are also found selling it at a
higher rate in comparison to the rates
prescribed by Government; and
(d) if so, the number of such dealers
detected so far and the action taken against
them, till date?
Petroleum smuggling
*32. SHRI SANJAY RAUT: Will the
Minister of  PETROLEUM AND
NATURAL GAS be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government's attention has
been drawn to the recent reports regarding
growing number of petroleum smuggling

10
business operations in the country,
particularly in western coastal line;
(b) if so, Government's response
thereto; and
(c) the details of steps taken or proposed
to be taken against such illicit petroleum
smuggling in the country?
Production of natural gas from gas
hydrates
*33. SHRIMATI  N.P. DURGA: Will
the Minister of  PETROLEUM AND
NATURAL GAS be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that recently huge
gas hydrates in Krishna-Godavari basin
have been discovered;
(b) whether it is also a fact that India is
looking at producing natural gas from gas
hydrates on commercial basis;
(c) if so, whether India has got that
technology since such a technology i.e.,
producing natural gas from gas hydrates, is
not available in any part of the world; and
(d) if so, the details thereof?
Profit earned by OMCs
*34. SHRI CHITTABRATA
MAJUMDAR:
SHRI TAPAN KUMAR SEN:
Will the Minister of  PETROLEUM
AND NATURAL GAS be pleased to state:
(a) the net profits earned by public
sector Oil Marketing Companies (OMCs)
during 2005-06, 2004-05, 2003-04;
(b) the net profit by the OMCs during
2001-02, 2000-01, 1999-2000;
(c) the profits by private stand alone
oil refineries during the above period; and
(d) the average crude price during these
years?
Constitution of Sixth Pay
Commission
*35. SHRI SHANT ARAM
LAXMAN NAIK:
SHRI LALIT SURI:
Will the Minister of  FINANCE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government propose to
constitute Sixth Pay Commission;
(b) by what date the same is likely to be
constituted; and
(c) the details of proposed terms of
reference of the Commission?
Preservation and promotion of tribal
culture
*36. SHRI BALAVANT ALIAS  BAL
APTE:
SHRI SHREEGOPAL VYAS:
Will the Minister of  CULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have prepared
any action plan for the preservation and
promotion of languages, folk dances, art
and culture of the tribals in the country;
(b) if so, the details thereof, State-wise;
and
(c) the details of the financial assistance
given to various agencies/NGOs by
Government for the purpose during the last
three years?

11
Relief package to coffee growers
*37. SHRIMATI  BRINDA KARAT:
Will the Minister of  FINANCE be pleased
to state:
(a) whether Government have
announced any relief package to coffee
growers in the year 2004-05, which waived
off two years interest due to those who
availed loans under Special Coffee Term
Loan (SCTL) scheme;
(b) if so, the details of the same; and
(c) how many small coffee growers have
benefited from this scheme?
Discovery of new gas hydrate
*38. SHRI ABU ASIM AZMI: Will the
Minister of  PETROLEUM AND
NATURAL GAS be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have
discovered huge quantity of ‘Gas Hydrate’
at Krishna and Godavari basin in Bay of
Bengal, recently;
(b) if so, the expected quantity of the
same and how it shall be utilized particularly
natural gas and L.P.G.; and
(c) at what position is the progress to
convert this gas into natural gas and L.P.G.?
Rise in inflation rate
*39. SHRI C. RAMACHANDRAIAH:
Will the Minister of  FINANCE be pleased
to state:
(a) whether inflation rate in the country
during the current  fiscal has been higher as
compared to that of during the last three
years;
(b) if so, the inflation rate during each
of the last three years, month-wise;
(c) whether steep increase has been
registered in the prices of daily food items
and fuels during the current fiscal;
(d) if so, the extent of increase registered
in the prices of said commodities with the
reasons therefor; and
(e) the steps taken/being taken by
Government to bring down the inflation
rate and to check the price rise of essential
commodities?
Misuse of funds by oil companies
*40. SHRI KARNENDU
BHATTACHARJEE: Will the Minister of
PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Comptroller
and Auditor General (CAG) has pointed
out glaring misuse of funds and irregularities
in accounts by the Ministry and State-
owned Oil Companies in the last ten
financial years;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) whether action is proposed to be
taken against those responsible for misuse
of funds and irregularities?
NEW DELHI; YOGENDRA NARAIN,
The 19th July, 2006 Secretary-General.

Total number of questions — 90
Incentives for airline operators
76. SHRI VIJAY J. DARDA:
SHRIMATI SHOBHANA
BHARTIA:
Will  the Minister of  CIVIL
AVIATION  be pleased to state:
(a) whether  his Ministry is planning to
come out with a five-year incentive package
for airline operators that link metros with
regional centres;
(b) if so, whether he declared that
incentives would be in the form of waiver
of certain airport user, parking, route
navigation and landing charges;
(c) whether the Ministry urged the
States to identify airstrips that are not in
use and develop them  through public-
private participation;
(d) whether the Ministry identified 35
non-metro airports for development and
Planning Commission has approved 10
airports; and
(e) if so, by when final decision is likely
to be taken in this regard?
Irrigation proposals received from
Andhra Pradesh
77. SHRIMATI N.P. DURGA: Will the
Minister of WATER RESOURCES be
pleased to state:
(a) the details of proposals submitted
by the State Government of Andhra
Pradesh to the Central Government meant
for irrigation clearance during the last two
years;
(b) the details of proposals/projects
approved or cleared by various authorities
of Government;
(c) the details of proposals/projects
pending for clearance in various
departments in the Central Government;
and
(d) the reasons for delay in clearing the
said proposals?

20
Revenue earned by AAI
78. SHRI VINAY KATIYAR:
SHRI BALAVANT ALIAS BAL
APTE:
Will the Minister of CIVIL  AVIATION
be pleased to state:
(a) the revenue earned by the Airports
Authority of India (AAI) from Delhi and
Mumbai airports separately during each of
the last two years;
(b) whether all the private airlines
operating in those airports have not paid
their dues to the AAI;
(c) if so, the details thereof; and
(d) the steps being taken by the AAI to
recover the dues from the private airlines
before the proposed restructuring of these
airports are implemented?
Merger of Air India  and Indian
79. SHRIMATI S.G. INDIRA: Will the
Minister of CIVIL  AVIATION  be pleased
to state:
(a) whether  it is a fact  that the Air
India Board had short listed consortia to
prepare a road map for merger of Air India
and Indian;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether the short  listed consortia
had submitted any detailed terms of
reference; and
(d) if so, the details thereof?
Disinvestment of Government stake
in Air India and Indian
80. SHRI  C. RAMACHANDRAIAH:
Will the Minister of CIVIL  AVIATION
be pleased to state:
(a) whether  Government have decided
to disinvest a portion of its equity in Air
India and Indian;
(b) if so, the amount of equity in both
airlines proposed to be disinvested;
(c) by when these are likely to be
disinvested; and
(d) the profit/loss position of these airlines
during 2004-2005 and first quarter of 2005-
2006?
Modernisation of Kolkata and
Chennai Airports
81. SHRIMATI S.G. INDIRA : Will
the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION  be
pleased to state:
(a) whether  it is a fact that there has
been stiff  opposition to the joint venture route
for modernisation of the Kolkata and
Chennai airports;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether Government are considering
to modernise these airports through AAI; and
(d) if so, the details thereof?
New airport in Orissa

PANY: Will the Minister of CIVIL
AVIATION  be pleased to state:
(a) whether there has been any demand
to construct an airpport at Jharsuguda in
Orissa; and
(b) if so, the steps taken by Government
so far in this regard?
Upgradation of Nagpur Airport
†83. SHRI DATTA MEGHE: Will the
Minister of  CIVIL AVIATION  be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is a fact  that Airports
Aurhority of India have prepared a
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

21
blueprint for upgradation of Nagpur
Airport to international level;
(b) if so, by when  this scheme would
be put into action; and
(c) the reasons for non-implementation
of this scheme so far?
Upgradation of airports into
International Airports
84. SHRI JANARDHANA
POOJARY: Will the Minister of CIVIL
AVIATION  be pleased to state:
(a) whether a number of airports in the
country have been identified for upgradation
into international airports;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether additional infrastructure
and facilities, like construction of a new
terminal building, second runway, etc., have
been carried out to meet the growing
passenger traffic at the Mangalore Airport,
thereby meeting the requirements of an
international airport;

consider upgrading Mangalore Airport into
an international airport; and
(e) if so, the details thereof and if not,
the reasons therefor?
Installation of landing instruments at
airports
85. SHRI JANARDHANA
POOJARY: Will the Minister of CIVIL
AVIATION  be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that each year
during  monsoon and winter, flight operation
becomes difficult, resulting in severe
disruption in schedule of almost every flight
leading to chaos at the airports;
(b) if so, the details in this regard;
(c) whether it is also a fact that
appropriate equipment to guide the aircrafts
during such seasons is unavailable in most
of the airports; and
(d) if so, by when such equipments
would be installed in all the airports, with
special reference to Mangalore Airport?
Enhancement of flying hours of pilots
86. SHRI C. PERUMAL: Will the
Minister of CIVIL AVIATION  be pleased
to state:
(a) whether there is any move to increase
the annual limit of 1000 flying hours for pilots;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether Government are aware that
proposed move  will be dangerous as it
would put more  stress on pilots; and
(d) if so, the final decision in this regard?
Air service between Bagdogra and
Kathmandu
†87. SHRI SAMAN PATHAK: Will
the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION  be
pleased to state:
(a) whether any proposal to introduce
air service between Bagdogra and
Kathmandu is under Government's
consideration;
(b) if so, the likelihood of the
implementation of the said proposal; and
(c) if not, the reasons therefor?
Agreement with US on airport
modernisation
88. SHRIMATI SHOBHANA
BHARTIA : W ill the Minister of CIVIL
AVIATION  be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have approved
the signing of an agreement between India
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

22
and US to enable the Indian civil aviation
bodies to get American assistance in
modernising aviation infrastructure,
technology and training;
(b) if so, whether any MoU was reached
with US Federal Aviation Authority for
developing and modernising airports and
other  infrastructure in managerial,
operational and technical areas;
(c) if so, the details of the agreeement;
(d) by when it is likely to be
implemented; and
(e) whether US had already signed such
agreement with more than 100 countries?
Bird hit cases at airports
89. DR. M.A.M. RAMASWAMY:
Will the Minister of  CIVIL AVIATION
be pleased to state:
(a) whether  there have been a number
of bird hit incidents at different airports in
the country endangering the lives of
passengers;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) the steps taken by Government to
stop such incidents?
Maintenance of aircrafts
90. SHRI ABU ASIM AZMI: Will the
Minister of CIVIL AVIATION  be pleased
to state:
(a) whether Government are well aware
that these days the civil aircrafts are not
properly checked before  taking off;
(b) if so, the details of the cases where
the complaints of tyre bursts of such
aircrafts have come to the notice of
Government  during the  last six months;
(c) the action taken against  the persons
responsible for negligence in the
performance of their duty; and
(d) what steps are proposed to be taken
for proper maintenance and checking of the
civil aircrafts in future?
Expenditure on Commercial Pilot
licence
91. SHRIMATI N.P. DURGA: Will the
Minister of CIVIL AVIATION  be pleased
to state:
(a) what is the total expenditure that
Government will incur on each student who
wishes to acquire commercial pilot licence
in India;
(b) the details of institutions, both in
public and private sector, that are providing
commercial pilot licence course in the
country, State-wise;
(c) what  is the approximate
expenditure that a student has to shell out
to get commercial pilot licence in any
private  institution;
(d) whether there is any control of
Government on private institutions about
fee structure and fulfilling the mandatory
flying requirement of 200 to 250 hours;
and
(e) if so, the details thereof?
Action against vanishing companies
†92. SHRI JAI PARKASH
AGGARWAL: Will the Minister of
COMPANY AFFAIRS be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Central Government are
contemplating to make stringent provisions
in the new company law against those fake
companies which disappear after making
loss of crores of rupees to investors;
(b) if so, the details thereof as on date;
(c) the latest status of this proposal;
and
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

23
(d) by when these amendments are
likely to be carried out?
Action against micro-finance
 companies
93. SHRI RAVULA CHANDRA
SEKAR REDDY: Will the Minister of
FINANCE be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are aware that
many poor people are facing many hardships
from the micro-finance companies;
(b) if so, the details of such micro finance
companies against whom Government have
taken action so far; and
(c) the steps being taken by Government
to protect the poor people from such
companies in future?
Director General of ASI
94. SHRIMATI SYEDA ANWARA
TAIMUR:
SHRI VIJAY J. DARDA:
Will the Minister of CULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) since how long the post of the
Director General of the Archaeological
Survey of India has been held by Indian
Administrative Service officers;
(b) whether the ASI has been declared
by Government as a scientific and technical
organization;
(c) whether at one time or another
important culture institutions like the National
Museum and the National Gallery of Modern
Art have been headed by I.A.S. officers;
(d) if so, the details thereof; and
(e) whether Government propose to
consider all options including amending of
the recruitment rules, so that the practice of
having I.A.S. officers on scientific, technical
and cultural institution is stopped?
Declaration of ASI as Scientific and
Technical Department
95. SHRIMATI MOHSINA
KIDWAI:
SHRI VIJAY J. DARDA:
Will the Minister of CULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) when was the notification declaring
the Archaeological Survey of India a
Scientific and Technical Department issued
by Government;
(b) what are the financial and
administrative implications of declaring a
Department as Scientific and Technical;
(c) whether the benefit and privileges
of a Scientific and Technical Department
have been fully extended to the
Archaeological Survey of India, and if not,
the reasons therefor; and
(d) by when the Archeological Survey
of India is likely to get all the benefits and
privileges of a Scientific and Technical
Department?
Observance of India-China
 friendship year
96. KUMARI NIRMALA
DESHPANDE: Will the Minister of
CULTURE be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are having any
special plan to observe this year in a
befitting way, to strengthen the age-old
friendship as this year is being observed as
India-China friendship year;
(b) what kind of cultural exchanges are
going to take place; and
(c) if not, the reasons therefor?

24
Historical discoveries in Krishna
District of Andhra Pradesh
97. SHRIMATI  N.P. DURGA: Will
the Minister of CULTURE be pleased to
state:
(a) whether it is a fact that three
Buddhist Chaityas and a Monastery, a
three dimensional structure, broken images,
pillars and pottery from the first and second
century AD have been found in Krishna
District of Andhra Pradesh;
(b) if so, the details of the discovery
by ASI;
(c) whether it is also a fact that
Ghantasala village of Krishna District was
first reported a historical site by Buswell of
East India Company in 1870-71; and
(d) if so, what has been done by
Government to excavate this area for more
historical discoveries?
Centrally protected monuments in
Andhra Pradesh
98. SHRI C. RAMACHANDRAIAH:
Will the Minister of CULTURE be pleased
to state:
(a) the Centrally protected monuments
in various districts of Andhra Pradesh;
(b) the amount spent on the
construction, preservation and maintenance
of those monuments during each of the last
three years;
(c) whether the State Government of
Andhra Pradesh has requested the Ministry
to include some more monuments located
in various districts as Centrally protected;
and
(d) if so, the action taken thereon?
Construction work of Udai Shankar
Natya Kala Academy in Almora
†99. SHRI HARISH RAWAT: Will the
Minister of CULTURE be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are aware that
the construction work of Udai Shankar
Natya Kala Academy in Almora
(Uttaranchal) has been stalled for the last
one year;
(b) whether any time-limit has been set
for the construction of this Academy; and
(c) if so, by when this construction
work is likely to be completed?
Loan for Andhra Pradesh from Japan
Bank
100. SHRIMATI N.P. DURGA: Will
the Minister of FINANCE be pleased to
state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the State
Government of Andhra Pradesh has sought
Rs. 3,560 crores loan from Japan Bank for
International Cooperation and for this
purpose requested the Central Government
for giving clearance from the Ministry and
the Planning Commission;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) what action the Ministry has taken
to clear the proposal?
RBI's clamp down on borrowing from
overseas corporate bodies
101. SHRI C. PERUMAL: Will the
Minister of FINANCE be pleased to state:
(a) whether private insurance companies
face difficulties in view of the Reserve Bank
of India's clamp down on borrowing from
overseas corporate bodies;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

25
(c) whether this will have effect on
insurance penetration to global level as
necessary capital will not be available?
Loans to farmers at seven per cent
interest rate
†102. SHRI MOTILAL VORA:
MS. SUSHILA TIRIYA:
 Will the Minister of FINANCE be
pleased to state:
(a) the details of farmers who have been
provided loans by the banks at the rate of
seven per cent alongwith the amount of
said loan upto June, 2006 after
Governments'  announcement of providing
short-term loan to the farmers at the rate of
seven per cent;
(b) whether Government are aware that
Co-operative banks have shown their
inability to provide loans to the farmers at
the rate of seven per cent; and
